Safety requirements emphasize data integrity, historical preservation, and comprehensive tracking across multiple classes and semesters. Efficiency requirements focus on system responsiveness and resource optimization for the same functional domains. The core conflict emerges in how these concerns manifest: Safety prioritizes complete, auditable attendance records with fault tolerance mechanisms, while Efficiency seeks minimal latency in marking attendance and generating reports. Both agents recognize the same functional requirements but frame them through different quality attribute lenses. The requirement to 'maintain historical attendance data' (SAF-L2-001-02) directly supports safety through auditability, while EFF-L2-002-01 views the same requirement through performance optimization. Teacher marking operations (SAF-L2-001-04, EFF-L2-002-03) must balance data validation rigor against marking speed. Student record viewing (SAF-L2-001-05, EFF-L2-002-04) requires secure access without latency penalties. Report generation (SAF-L2-001-01/06, EFF-L2-002-05) must maintain accuracy while achieving acceptable query performance.
